issues.title: [Bug]: local variable is in scope inside its own initializer (self-recursive closure crashes at runtime / INTERNAL_ERROR)
issues.output:
typed: error: interface conversion: values.BalValue is nil, not *values.Function at main(a1.bal:5)
var: fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: expression type not resolved --> a2.bal:5:38
int z = z + 1: error: unsupported type combination: <nil> + int64 at main(a3.bal:4)
issues.edge_case_reason: Self-reference to a local inside its own initializer (self-recursive closure / `int z = z + 1`) is invalid, unusual code.
issues.reasoning: All three variants reproduce on main 1bcb85b9. Clean-context spec check: §7.11 says the scope of a local-var-decl starts immediately after the statement, so the self-reference is an undefined symbol and every variant must be a compile error. Nutcracker's symbol resolution puts the variable in scope too early: two variants compile to invalid BIR and fail at runtime, and the `var` variant gives INTERNAL_ERROR. Frontend (missing diagnostic + internal error). Not a duplicate: #1423 has the same INTERNAL_ERROR text but a different trigger (annotation on local var).

issues.title: [Bug]: remote method of a client object with return type `never` is not rejected
issues.output: Both compile and run with no output (exit 0); no diagnostic reported.
issues.edge_case_reason: Declaring a client remote method with return type `never` is a rarely used construct.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main 1bcb85b9: both programs are accepted. Clean-context spec check: §5.6.3.4 says 'The return type of the remote method of a client object must not be never', a static constraint on the declaration, so both must be compile errors. Missing semantic diagnostic, so frontend. No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: `c ? x is int : y` is misparsed as qualified identifier `int:` (syntax error or INTERNAL_ERROR "Unexpected builtin type kind")
issues.output:
c1: fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: Unexpected builtin type kind --> c1.bal:4:17 (at `int`)
c2: error[SYNTAX_ERROR]: missing slash asterisk token --> c2.bal:6:33
issues.edge_case_reason: A type test against a builtin type as the middle operand of an ordinary conditional expression is common code.
issues.reasoning: Both variants reproduce on main 1bcb85b9. Clean-context spec check: a qualified identifier uses NoSpaceColon, which allows no whitespace around ':'. The ternary uses a literal ':'. `is` binds tighter than ?:. So `b ? x is int : x is string` is valid, and the programs should print `yes` and `false`. The parser wrongly treats `int :` / `string :` as a module prefix: a bogus syntax error in one case and INTERNAL_ERROR in the other. Frontend (parser). Related to #1726 (another NoSpaceColon parse problem, different construct), but not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: tcp:Caller passed to a tcp service fails `is tcp:Caller`
issues.reproducer: (issue's program; requires ballerina/tcp, which exists only on unmerged PR #701)
issues.output: Not runnable on main 1bcb85b9: lib/stdlibs/ballerina has no tcp module. PR #701 (feat(tcp): port ballerina/tcp standard library) is still open and unmerged.
issues.reasoning: Standard library (ballerina/tcp) issue, so category library + triage-lib. It cannot be reproduced on main because ballerina/tcp is not merged yet (it lives on open PR #701). The expected behaviour is clearly valid: a value passed as a `tcp:Caller` parameter must belong to `tcp:Caller`, and the issue explains the cause (native code builds the object with the top `object` type). The fix depends on #1797 (open). You may prefer to keep it attached to PR #701 rather than treat it as a main-branch bug.

issues.title: [Bug]: self.init() in a class without an init method re-runs field initializers
issues.output:
1   (expected 5)
BIR: class N `init()` body contains `self[x] = 1` (field initializer), and reset() calls `self.init()`
issues.edge_case_reason: Explicitly calling self.init() from an ordinary method of a class with no declared init is a rarely used construct.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main 1bcb85b9 (prints 1). Clean-context spec check: §8.6 makes field initialization a separate step from calling init, and §6.8.1.5 says a missing init is equivalent to an empty one and may be called via self. So the program prints 5, or under a stricter reading it is rejected at compile time. Printing 1 is wrong under both readings. The dumped BIR folds the field initializers into the user-callable `init` method, so the BIR is wrong for the source: frontend (BIR gen). Related to #1252 (init in object shape; its fix would make this a compile error), #1572 and #1592, but not a duplicate.
